For David, to make known the grace of this ointment, says: "You are fairer in form than the sons of men; grace is poured upon your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever. Gird your sword upon your thigh, O most mighty, in your comeliness and your beauty; set out, go forward prosperously and reign, because of truth and gentleness and justice, and your right hand shall lead you wonderfully. Your arrows are sharp, O most mighty; peoples shall fall beneath you, into the heart of the king's enemies. Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is an upright scepter. You have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions. Myrrh and stacte and cassia are from your garments, from the ivory palaces, out of which they have gladdened you."

We have looked into the secrets of the immortal ointment, and the order of the divine plan has been shown to us: an everlasting kingdom and the crown of heaven were conferred on our Lord together with the majesty of the ointment. But who this is that has received the power to rule the world, and who is adorned with the majesty of a venerable name, another oracle shows us, for the same David says: "Why have the nations raged, and the peoples devised vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ." Why do you exalt yourself so, sacrilegious persuasion? Why do you ensnare wretched people with unbridled recklessness? The ointment of Christ grants the kingdom of heaven; your ointment stirs up the flames of Gehenna.

But what that priest frames with his impure mouth and the defilement of his polluted words, it is worth examining with careful inquiry. He urges his fellows to be of good cheer because their god has been set free, and to hold fast to the confidence of good hope. Oh, in what wretched, what mournful snares this perishing cunning entangles itself! Who sets your god free? For whom has he accomplished what he labors at? Learn, learn what you do not know, learn what you do not see:

Christ, the Son of God, in order to free the human race from the snares of death, truly endured all these things: to lift the yoke of harsh captivity, to restore man to the Father, to appease the offense and reconcile man with God in a happy reconciliation, and to show by his own example the fruit of the promised resurrection. The Son of God did what he had promised beforehand. He broke through the gates of the infernal abode and, trampling death underfoot, overthrew the compulsion of a harsh law. Over three days the throng of the righteous was reviewed by him and gathered together, so that the wickedness of death should no longer lord it over them, and so that the merit of the righteous should not collapse through long despair. He broke the everlasting bars, and at Christ's command the iron doors fell down. See, the earth trembled, and, shaken in the stability of its foundations, it recognized the divine power of Christ present there. Before the appointed time the whirling motion of the world hastens the day on, and the sun, before completing the span of the daylight hours, hurries its course and sinks toward night. See, the top of the veil is split, and the gloom of night hides the world in deeper darkness. All the elements were thrown into turmoil while Christ fought, that is, when for the first time he armed a human body against the tyranny of death. For three days the battle was fought in this conflict, until death, its malicious strength overcome, was broken.

Why, with your usual impatience, you devout man, you man of Christ, do you despair and lose heart? Can you not bear a delay of three days? Do you confess your anxiety and despair in fresh prayers? That you would do this on that day the Holy Spirit indicates with his venerable voice, when he says through David: "We are counted as sheep for the slaughter. Arise; why do you sleep, O Lord? Arise, and do not cast us off for ever. Why do you turn away your face? Do you forget our poverty and our affliction? For our soul is brought low to the dust; our belly cleaves to the ground. Arise, O Lord, help us, and deliver us for your name's sake."

See, after three days a day dawns brighter than usual, and the sun has its former light restored to it. Christ, the almighty God, is worshipped with the sun's more brilliant rays; the saving Godhead exults, and the throng of the righteous and the saints accompanies his triumphal chariot. Then mortality, raised up, cries out in exalted joy: "Where, O death, is your sting?" Then the saving Godhead, going on ahead, commands the heavenly gates to be opened to him: "Open, open, and tear away the immortal bars! Christ, God, having trampled death underfoot, is bringing back to heaven the man he had taken up." This is foretold by the venerable prophet with holy voice, and from the prophet's mouth is heard the voice of the one who commands; for the Holy Spirit, to show us the authority of Christ as he commands, says: "Lift up your gates, you princes, and be lifted up, you eternal gates, and the King of glory shall come in."

This command is given to angels who do not know, for they could not know when the Word of God came down to earth. So they too answer with an anxious question: "Who is this King of glory?" To their question Christ replies plainly in the majesty of his Godhead: "The Lord strong and mighty, the Lord mighty in battle." At once the Son of God is recognized by the guardians of heaven, and they understand whatever had escaped them before. They see the spoils of the vanquished enemy, and, recalling the order of the original plan, they too cry out together, with repeated voice, along with those who are ascending: "Lift up your gates, you who are set over them, and be lifted up, you eternal gates, and the King of glory shall come in."

When the Son returned, the Father restored to him the promised scepter of the kingdom and granted him the throne of the kingdom with equal power, that he might command, hold the kingdom, and rule in the everlasting majesty of his Godhead. Hear what the Holy Spirit bade Daniel say about him: "I saw in a vision by night, and behold, in the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he came to the Ancient of Days and stood in his presence, and those who stood by brought him forward; and there was given to him royal power and the kingdom and all glory, and all the kings of the earth shall serve him, and his power is everlasting, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed."

These same things are shown to us by holy revelation, for we find it written thus in the Apocalypse: "And I turned and looked to see the voice that was speaking with me, and I saw seven golden lampstands, and in the midst of the lampstands one like a son of man, clothed in a robe reaching to the feet and girded about the breast with a golden sash. His head and his hair were white as white wool, as snow; his eyes were like a flame of fire, and his feet were like brass, as if from a fiery furnace, and his voice was like the sound of many waters. In his right hand he held seven stars, and from his mouth came a sharp two-edged sword, and his face shone like the sun in its strength. And when I saw him, I fell at his feet as though dead, and he laid his right hand upon me, saying: Do not be afraid; I am the first and the last, and the living one; I was dead, and behold, I am alive for ever and ever,

and I hold the keys of death and of the underworld." After his resurrection, too, when he was giving sure commands to his disciples, he concluded the series of his immortal commands with this law: "All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you." And that God the Father, making him a partner in the kingdom, granted him a seat on the royal throne is taught by this oracle: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet. The Lord shall send forth the scepter of your power from Zion, and you shall rule in the midst of your enemies. With you is sovereignty in the day of your power, in the splendor of the saints; from the womb, before the morning star, I begot you. The Lord has sworn and will not repent."

These are the enemies of God, most sacred Emperors, who throw the order of truth into confusion with a contrary law, who at the prompting of perverse desire conceive sacrilegious vows, who in the frenzy of a profane mind are forever worshipping either wood or stone. Having reached this point, we ought to lay open the order of the holy plan, so that whatever the prophetic teaching has handed down to us, as we search out the holy word of God, may be set out specifically to refute the stains of profane error; lest, if, as we have said, those who handed down sacrileges to the erring invented them, the order of truth should likewise be sought out by us too inquisitively [?]. So, setting the rest aside for a little while, let our discourse turn to setting out these things, which are true.

My lord emperors, lend me the patience of your sacred ears, so that I may set out for your clemency the whole of what we promise. Why God, that is, the Son of God, consented to become man will be shown to your piety by a brief and true account. When God made the first man, Adam, in his own image, he gave him a fixed law of commandments. Adam was deceived through a woman, Eve, by the persuasions of the devil, and lost the dignity of the glory promised him. It was a tree in paradise that lost him the favor of the rewards God had promised.

Man was made from the clay of virgin earth, for, as Scripture says, it had not yet rained upon the earth. By despising God's commandments, he bound the human race in the snares of mortality. All this had to be reformed and corrected, and the reforming of the origin had to reshape the beginnings. Adam, made from the clay of virgin earth, lost by his own transgression the life promised to him. Christ, born through the Virgin Mary and the Holy Spirit, received both immortality and a kingdom. A tree offered deadly food to those it deceived; the wood of the cross restored life in an immortal bond. Adam showed contempt, Christ obeyed God. So by divine dispensation, whatever Adam lost, Christ found.

For after long ages, in the last spans of time, that is, almost in the last week of the ages, the Word of God mingled himself with a human body, to set man free, to conquer death, and to join the frailty of the human body to divine immortality. For what would so great a throng of saints have done? What hope of salvation would they have had? What reward for their merits, if they too were held bound under one and the same lot in the inescapable snares of mortality? Abel, Enos, Noah, Shem, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob could have promised themselves nothing from God's mercy and majesty. After such merit of faith they too would have gone the way of all the rest, condemned alike. One ruin of death would have taken in all God's saints, and piety would have had no reward with God, if one and the same condition of death swallowed up all.

But God had promised Abraham a kingdom brighter than the stars of heaven. That is why the Virgin Mary, descended from Abraham's line, conceived God: so that the offspring of the men named above might be joined in the bond of an immortal fellowship, and so that the human race, united in an equal partnership through one who is at once man and God, might by the merit of obedience come to the dominion of immortality. Since, most sacred emperors, we have now satisfied curious ears, let us pursue the rest, so that in this way too our discourse may cleanse the filth of polluted ears and purge them.

There follows yet another symbol, which is handed on as something great to the credulous ears of wretched men: "The bull is the dragon's father, and the dragon the bull's father." At times, devil, you have betrayed to us the signs of your stained name; at times you have confessed your infamous name with your own voice. I know who you were and what you dared; I know what the malicious persuasion of your crimes has done. This is what you were so eagerly promising Eve when you were ruining her, saying to her: "You will be like gods." Even then you were preparing temples for yourself and your own, building shrines, and consecrating the filth of your poisoned mouth with wicked rites.

You creep about in temples and feed on the wretched blood of slaughtered victims. Your venom has never lacked gore, nor the half-burnt parts of cremated bodies. You have often bloodied yourself with the blood of human victims too, and your frenzy and the venom of your parched throat were fed on the gore of the temple of Latiaris or the altar of Carthage. Doing these things, you boast that you help wretched men, so that you may destroy them by your cruelty, deceive them by your persuasion, and lay them low by your promises. That is how you look after your own, you parricide! Flee, wretched men, flee, and abandon that contagion with all the speed you can. It is a dragon that is worshipped. It cannot hide; it has itself confessed the true meaning of its name, and punishment follows the defendant who confesses.

Hear what the holy prophet proclaims at God's prompting. Faith has handed down to us this oracle of Isaiah, for he says: "On that day God will bring his holy, great and mighty sword upon the dragon, the great and twisting serpent, and he will slay the dragon." God's will is the very substance of a finished work. Sentence has been passed on the dragon's death; whatever God has said is done. The dying dragon's only consolation is that a large crowd of the lost will accompany his ruin. If you ask the day of his death: he was struck down when he saw God as man, when the divinity of Christ appeared to us.

After that day, whoever has followed the ways of this serpent must die with the serpent. He himself fashioned these gods you worship; he himself put them together. If your stubborn minds remain in this error, you too will burn together with your gods, so that whatever your founders earned by divine punishment will, through your fellowship with them, pass over to your ruin as well. Believe me, the devil has left nothing undone that might weaken or destroy wretched man. That is why he changes himself through every shape in endless variety, and why he has armed himself with cunning of every kind: so that he may snare men in varied and manifold frauds and kill them.

The abandoned executioner (oh, the wickedness of it!) arranged that his rites should always be renewed by means of a tree. He knew that the life of man would be fastened to the wood of the cross and bound in the bond of everlasting immortality, so he meant to deceive men doomed to perish with an imitation of that wood. In the Phrygian rites, which they call the rites of the Mother of the gods, a pine tree is cut down every year, and an image of a young man is tied to the middle of the tree. In the rites of Isis a trunk is cut from a pine tree, and the middle of this trunk is carefully hollowed out; there an idol of Osiris, made from the cuttings, is buried. In the rites of Proserpina a tree is cut down and fashioned into the likeness

and shape of a virgin. When it has been brought into the city it is mourned for forty nights, and on the fortieth night it is burned. The other trees I mentioned are consumed by a similar flame, for after a year the flame devours the pyre of these trees too. You have erred, wretch, and erred greatly. That fire can do you no good. In vain you flatter yourself with that flame, forever renewing this fire with your inventions. The fire that exacts punishment for your crimes rages on in an endless succession of torments.

Learn the order of the divine and liberating wood, so that you may know that nothing can help you. A wooden ark freed the human race from the flood. Abraham laid wood on the shoulders of his only son. A wooden rod protected the people of God as they left Egypt. Wood gave back a sweet taste to the bitter springs of Marah. By a wooden rod saving water was brought forth from the spiritual rock. To defeat Amalek, Moses stretched out his hands along a rod. The patriarch dreamed of an angel leaning on a wooden ladder and saw some going up it and others coming down. And the law of God was entrusted to a wooden ark. All this happened so that through these things, as if by steps, the salvation of men might arrive at the wood of the cross. Therefore the wood of the cross holds up the fabric of heaven, strengthens the foundations of the earth, and leads to life those who are fastened to it. The devil's wood always burns and dies, and with its ashes it carries those who believe in it down to the depths of Tartarus.

Let us also consider carefully what the following is. When the devil consecrates his tree, he has a ram sacrificed at dead of night at the roots of the felled tree. Who persuaded you of this, wicked one? Where did you learn this with your pestilent greed? Do you always set yourself against the supreme God out of wicked desire? That is why the stern judgment of the Godhead hurls you down from heaven in a ruinous fall, and why God's sentence decrees perpetual punishment for you: because every day a new crime is added to your crimes, and because you try to deceive God's man with fraudulent persuasion. See what the mocking enemy has devised for himself! When Abraham was about to sacrifice his son, at God's command a ram was put in his place and was caught at the roots of a nearby tree.

When the supreme God was about to free his people from the tyranny of the Egyptians, he ordered a ram to be killed at night and commanded that the doorposts be smeared with its blood. He ordered it to be eaten by a fixed number of people at a night meal, and he gave the sacrifice itself the name Passover. But the providence of the divine majesty devised this as an image of things to come, to show us the true Passover through signs. So when the prophet, at the bidding of the divine Spirit, foretold the passion of our Lord, he said: "Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer, so he did not open his mouth. In his humiliation justice was taken from him. Who will tell of his generation? For his life will be taken away from the earth."

Another prophet also gave the same answer in a similar oracle: "Lord, make it known to me, and I shall know; then I saw their schemes. I was led like an innocent lamb to the slaughter. They plotted against me, saying: Come, let us put wood into his bread, and let us wipe out his life from the earth."

That our Lord is called a lamb is shown to us by holy revelation. For in the Apocalypse we find it written thus: "And I saw, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures and among the elders, a Lamb standing as though slain, with seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out through all the earth. He came and took the book from the right hand of the one seated on the throne. When he had taken the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding golden harps and bowls full of the incense of supplications, which are the prayers of the saints. And they sang a new song, saying: Worthy are you to take the book and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you redeemed us for God out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, and you have made us a kingdom and priests for our God,

and we shall reign upon the earth." John too calls the Son of God by the name of lamb, so that he also answers to the prophetic promise. For he says in the Gospel: "On the next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who takes away the sins of the world." The venerable blood of this Lamb is shed for the salvation of men, so that the Son of God may redeem his saints by pouring out his precious blood, and so that those who are set free by the blood of Christ may first be consecrated by the majesty of immortal blood. Blood poured out before idols protects no one. So that the gore of cattle may not deceive or destroy wretched men, let it be said: that blood pollutes, it does not redeem, and through various misfortunes it drives men down to death. Wretched are those who are bloodied by the outpouring of sacrilegious blood. Why does the taurobolium or the criobolium drench you with a wicked stain of blood?

So let the filth you are gathering be washed away. Seek the noble springs, seek pure waters, so that there, after your many stains, the blood of Christ together with the Holy Spirit may make you white. But if full persuasion is to call wretched men back to a sound mind, greater authority is needed, so that once their minds have been cured and healed, no trace of the former plague is left.

What idols are, then, and what substance they have, has been shown by the mouth of the prophets and by the divine voice of God. All of this must be set out in detail, so that it may be recognized as something not put forward by our own rashness, but handed down to us by divine teaching and sealed by a heavenly voice. What their substance is, the venerable voice of Wisdom shows, for it says in the books of Solomon: "They thought all the idols of the nations to be gods, which have neither the use of eyes to see, nor nostrils to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers on their hands to handle things, and even their feet are useless for walking. For a man made them, and one whose breath is borrowed fashioned them. But no man can fashion a god like himself; for since he is mortal, what he fashions with lawless hands is dead. Yet he is better than the things he worships, since he at least has lived, but they never have." What more do we need? Wisdom has addressed us with a divine voice. She has taught whatever she had seen in the secrets of God and shown what is wholesome, so that frail and perishable mortality should not rush headlong to its own ruin and death.

The Holy Spirit gives the same warning in the Psalms, for we find it written thus in the hundred and thirty-fourth psalm: "The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths and do not speak; they have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear; nor is there any breath in their mouths. May those who make them become like them." If the craftsman who carved or cast an image to show off his skill is struck by the divine punishment of a curse, consider what the man should expect who calls a god what another man has sold.

Jeremiah too, when he was giving commandments to the people at God's bidding, addressed them with these words: "But say in your heart: It is you we must worship, O Lord. For my angel is with you, and I myself will search out your souls. Their tongue is polished by a craftsman; they themselves are overlaid with gold and silver, but they are false and cannot speak. As if for a girl who loves finery, they take gold and make crowns for the heads of their gods. And at times the priests take gold and silver from their gods and spend it on themselves; they will even give some of it to prostitutes. They dress them in garments like men, these gods of silver, gold and wood." He adds in what follows, to drive out every doubt and fear: "Owls and swallows, and birds likewise, fly over their bodies and heads. From this you will know that they are not gods; so do not fear them. For the gold they wear for show will not shine unless someone wipes off the tarnish; not even when they were being cast did they feel anything. They were bought at a price, things in which there is no breath; having no feet, they are carried on men's shoulders." He adds, too, so that the mind once strengthened may be made firmer still: "Knowing therefore from these things that they are not gods, do not fear them." And to show the wretched disgrace of their priests, he adds: "In their houses the priests sit with torn tunics, their heads and beards shaved and their heads bare. They roar, crying out before their gods like the dead in Gehenna."

That kings and nations too will pronounce these things about them, the same prophet declares with prophetic voice, for he says: "Afterwards it will be known to all nations and kings that they are false, for it is plain that they are not gods and that there is no work of God in them. They will not raise up a king for a country, nor give rain to men. They will not decide a case or deliver a country from wrong, for they can do nothing. And when fire breaks out in the house of the wooden gods, overlaid with gold and silver, their priests will escape, but the gods themselves will be burned up in the midst like beams. They will not withstand a king or a war. How then can anyone think or admit that they are gods? The wooden gods, overlaid with gold and silver, will not save themselves from thieves or robbers; strong men take from them the gold and silver they are covered with."

Take away, take away without fear, most sacred emperors, the ornaments of the temples. Let the fire of the mint or the flame of the smelting furnaces melt these gods down; transfer all their votive offerings to your own use and ownership. Since the destruction of the temples you have been advanced to greater heights by the power of God. You have conquered your enemies and extended the empire. And so that greater glory might be added to your valor, you changed and defied the order of the seasons: in winter, a thing that has never been done and never will be, you trod the swelling, raging waves of Ocean. Under your oars the waters of a sea almost unknown to us trembled, and the Briton quailed at the unexpected sight of an emperor. What more do you want? The very elements have been conquered and have yielded to your valor.

That God commands that idols not be made, the decrees of the sacred law declare. For in Exodus we find it written thus: "You shall not make for yourselves gods of silver or gods of gold." And again in the same book I find the voice of God commanding: "You shall not make for yourself an idol or a likeness of anything." The Holy Spirit puts the wretched to shame, because he wants to call back those who stray, not to destroy them, and he says through Isaiah: "Be utterly put to shame, you who trust in carved images, who say to cast images: You are our gods." He also gives a law for the consecrated people to keep with devotion forever, and commands thus: "You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone." And in Deuteronomy similar commandments of God are found, for he says: "You shall have no other gods besides me." He also adds, to impress the weight of his majesty upon their minds: "See, see that I am, and there is no god besides me. I will kill and I will make alive; I will strike and I will heal; and there is no one who can deliver from my hands."

In the Apocalypse too the same thing is shown by holy revelation, for it is written thus: "And I saw another angel flying in mid-heaven, with the eternal gospel to proclaim upon the earth to every nation and tribe and tongue and people. He said with a loud voice: Fear the Lord instead, and give him glory, for the hour of his judgment has come; and worship him who made heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them." Our Lord Jesus Christ too, keeping the ordinances of his Father's law, proclaims the same thing in a venerable decree, for he says: "Hear, O Israel: the Lord your God is one God. And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength. This is the first commandment. And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets."

This divine and venerable commandment of the immortal Lord is followed by a holy conclusion. To show the way of salvation more plainly, he adds these words: "And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true Lord, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent."

You know the order of the sacred commandments. You have learned from a venerable and immortal voice what you ought to follow and what you ought to flee. Hear now what ruin awaits those who despise them, and with what calamities the binding force of the venerable law has tied them. For the law sums up the close of the venerable commandments in these words:

“Whoever sacrifices to gods, and not to the Lord alone, shall be rooted out.” If the dreaded penalty struck only the sacrilegious man himself, if the severity of the law threatened only the one who sins, he might well steel himself for sacrilege in the recklessness of his stubborn madness. But now it threatens his stock and his offspring, and its aim is that no part of that most wicked seed be left, that no trace of the profane race remain: “Whoever sacrifices to gods,” it says, “shall be rooted out.” Consider what you are doing, you wretched and grievous delusion: your crime condemns a great many, it destroys a great many, and the penalty, multiplying, is spread through the whole substance of your race. Why the authority of the ordained law rages so fiercely against those who sacrifice is shown with clear meaning in Deuteronomy, for there we find it written: “They sacrificed to demons and not to God.” Do not go over to contaminated and polluted spirits; do not hope for help from inferior beings; do not make supplication to those whom, by the grace of God, you ought now to command.

See, this demon whom you worship trembles when he hears the name of God and of his Christ, and when he answers our questions he can scarcely put his trembling words together. Clinging to a man, he is torn, burned and beaten, and at once confesses the crimes he has committed. By the prohibition of the venerable law you are commanded not to worship him, not to make supplication to him, not to fall prostrate and bend your knees to him. Hence the severity of the penalty, hence the dreadful sentence of punishment: that, though God in his kindness has granted you freedom, you choose instead the yoke of slavery. The most high God does not cease to strike at this crime with his saving voice; rather, in his mercy he hastens to correct erring men with frequent warnings. Hear what the divine voice says through the prophet Isaiah: “They worshipped the gods that their own fingers made, and man was bowed down,

and man was humbled, and I will not forgive them.” Even you, O profane men, the angry Godhead addresses, and still confronts your errors with his holy voice; for he says further on through the same prophet: “To them you poured out libations, and on them you laid sacrifices: shall I not be angry at these things? says the Lord.” Still the saving God puts off his anger and holds back his severity, to see whether you may perhaps repent of your sin and in some way abandon the ruin of your sacrilegious will. See, in the very onrush of his anger he again persuades you with a gentle voice and restrains the goads of his wrath, for he says through the prophet Jeremiah: “Do not walk after strange gods to serve them, and do not worship them, lest you provoke me by the works of your hands to destroy you.”

Why are you so bent on sacrilege that you stop up your ears? Why do you hasten so, in the heat of your stubborn madness, toward your own ruin and death? God made you free; it is in your hands whether you live or perish. Why do you hurl yourself over the cliffs? Standing on a slippery path and already in the act of falling, at last check your stumbling steps. See, the sentence is pronounced; see, the penalty is decreed. Long has the divine forbearance spared your crimes; long has it looked upon your offence and pretended not to see. You are coming to that perilous point where hope and prayers fail. And so that you may be more plainly instructed, learn the ruin that punishment brings. On this matter the whole tenor of the answer is in the Apocalypse, for it is written thus: “If anyone worships the beast and its image and receives its mark on his forehead and on his hand, he too shall drink of the wine of God’s wrath, mixed in the cup of his anger, and he shall be punished with fire and sulphur before the eyes of the Lamb; and the smoke of their torments shall go up for ever and ever, and they shall have no rest day or night, whoever worship the beast and its image.”

But upon you too, most sacred Emperors, the duty is laid of avenging and punishing this evil, and it is enjoined on you by the law of the most high God that your severity should pursue the crime of idolatry in every way. Hear, and commit to your holy minds, what God commands concerning this crime. In Deuteronomy this law is written, for it says: “If your brother or your son or your wife, who is in your bosom, or your friend, who is as your own soul, should entreat you secretly, saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods, the gods of the nations,’ you shall not consent to him, nor listen to him, nor shall your eye spare him, nor shall you conceal him: you shall surely denounce him. Your hand shall be the first upon him to kill him, and afterwards the hand of all the people; and they shall stone him, and he shall die, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God.”

He commands that neither son nor brother be spared, and he drives the avenging sword through the beloved body of a wife. A friend too he pursues with lofty severity, and the whole people is armed to tear apart the bodies of the sacrilegious. Even upon whole cities, if they are caught in this crime, destruction is decreed. And so that your providence may learn this more plainly, I will set out the sentence of the established law. In the same book the Lord appointed a penalty for whole cities in these words, for he says: “Or if you hear it said in one of the cities which the Lord your God gives you to dwell in, ‘Let us go and serve other gods, whom you have not known,’ you shall surely put to death all who are in the city with the slaughter of the sword, and you shall burn the city with fire, and it shall be without inhabitant; it shall never be rebuilt, so that the Lord may turn away from the fury of his anger. And he will show you mercy and have pity on you and multiply you, if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God and keep

his commandments.” The most high God promises us, most sacred Emperors, the rewards of his mercy and decrees the increase of the greatest prosperity. Do, therefore, what he commands; fulfil what he enjoins. Your reign has been heaped with greater gifts; placed at the beginning of faith, you have felt the increase of divine favour. Never has the venerable hand of God forsaken you, never has it refused you help in your struggles: the wedges of your adversaries have been overthrown, and rebel arms have always fallen before your face; proud peoples have been sent under the yoke, the hopes of Persia have collapsed, and cruelty, weighed down by its own evils, could not long stand against you. You and they alike have felt the power of God, with differing outcomes: on you the crown of heavenly victory has been bestowed, and by your good fortune our hardships are relieved.

These rewards, most sacred Emperors, the most high God has given you in return for your faith; having recompensed you meanwhile with these honours, he invites you to the mysteries of the venerable law. With a pure mind, a devout conscience and an uncorrupted soul, let your Clemency ever look to heaven, ever await help from God, implore the venerable divinity of Christ, and offer spiritual victims to the saving God for the welfare of the whole world and for your own. So will all things turn out happily for you, victories, wealth, peace, plenty, health and triumphs, so that, borne forward by the divine majesty, you may govern the world with a prosperous reign.
